EDUCATION
Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA
S.B. Computer Science and Engineering (Course 6-3), expected June 2028
GPA 5.0/5.0
Coursework: 6.5840 Distributed Systems, 6.1810 Operating Systems, 6.1220 Design and Analysis of Algorithms, 6.5210 Advanced Algorithms, 18.650 Statistics for Applications, 6.1910 Computation Structures

EXPERIENCE
Citadel Securities, Chicago, IL
Quantitative Developer Intern, Options Market Making · June 2026 – August 2026
- Rewrote the per-underlying volatility-surface fitter on the equity options desk from Python to C++; fit time fell from 41 ms to 2.3 ms per update, allowing the desk to refit on every underlying tick rather than on a 100 ms timer.
- Built a replay harness that reconstructs order-book state from 1.2 TB/day of exchange feeds; used by three traders to backtest quoting parameter changes.
- Profiled the desk's Python research tooling and removed a serialization bottleneck; a typical end-of-day parameter sweep went from 55 minutes to 12.
- Received a return offer.

Jane Street, New York, NY
Software Engineering Intern · June 2025 – August 2025
- Implemented an incremental build-graph cache for the firm's OCaml monorepo build system; median incremental build time on the benchmark suite dropped 34%.
- Added structured tracing to the market-data normalization path and found a 7% CPU regression introduced two releases earlier; fix merged to production.
- Wrote the design note and the migration plan for rolling the cache out to the firm's second build cluster; adopted after the internship ended.
- Received a return offer.

MIT CSAIL, Parallel and Distributed Operating Systems group
Undergraduate Researcher · September 2025 – Present
- Working on a verified file-system crash-consistency checker; wrote the symbolic executor front end (about 6k lines of Rust) and found two previously unknown ordering bugs in an existing research file system.
- Presenting the checker at the group's weekly meeting; a workshop submission is planned for spring 2027.

PROJECTS
Sharded, linearizable key-value store (6.5840 final project, extended)
- Multi-Raft implementation in Go with dynamic shard rebalancing, lease-based reads and snapshot transfer; sustains 120k ops/s across 5 shards on a 15-node cluster and passes 2,000 consecutive runs of the course's fault-injection tests under the race detector.
- Extended the course spec with a Paxos-based configuration service and a formal TLA+ model of the reconfiguration protocol; model-checked to 9 steps with no invariant violations.

AWARDS
- ICPC North America Championship 2026: 1st place (team of 3); advanced to the ICPC World Finals
- William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition 2025: rank 71 of 3,988
- USA Computing Olympiad: Platinum division (2023)
- MIT Battlecode 2026: 5th place of 420 teams
- MIT Undergraduate Research Opportunities Program award (funded), 2025–26

TEACHING AND SERVICE
- Lab assistant, 6.1810 Operating Systems, Fall 2026
- Problem setter, MIT Informatics Tournament 2026
- Grader, 6.1220 Design and Analysis of Algorithms, Spring 2026

ACTIVITIES
- MIT Pokerbots 2025: 11th place of 230 teams
- Member, MIT Running Club

SKILLS
C++, Rust, Go, OCaml, Python · Linux systems programming, lock-free data structures, distributed consensus, TLA+ · Git, Bazel, perf, gdb
